name: Vietnamese Nguyễn Architecture
summary: Imperial architectural style of the Nguyễn Dynasty characterized by elaborate ornamentation, curved roofs, and Chinese-inspired elements.

name: Trullo
summary: Dry stone hut with conical roof found in the Puglia region of Italy.

name: Ethiopian Rock-Hewn Churches
summary: Monolithic churches carved directly into rock cliffs and mountains in northern Ethiopia.

name: Mississippian Platform Mound
summary: Earthen mound architecture characterized by flat-topped pyramids used for ceremonial platforms and elite residences.

name: Dutch Colonial Architecture
summary: A style blending Dutch architectural elements with local materials and techniques in colonial contexts.

name: Khrushchyovka
summary: A type of low-cost, prefabricated concrete panel housing constructed during the Nikita Khrushchev era to address urban housing shortages.

name: Central Asian Muqarnas
summary: A three-dimensional decorative element used in Islamic architecture, consisting of small niches stacked in tiers to create intricate honeycomb-like structures.

name: Vesara Hoysala style
summary: Distinctive temple architecture from the Hoysala Empire featuring star-shaped platforms and intricate carvings.

name: Kashan Merchant Houses
summary: Opulent residential architecture of wealthy Persian merchants featuring interior courtyards and intricate decorative elements.

name: Ksar Architecture
summary: A fortified village made of mudbrick common in the oases of the Sahara.

name: Brick Gothic
summary: A regional variation of Gothic architecture using brick instead of stone in areas lacking natural stone resources.

name: Manierismo Toscano
summary: Regional variant of Mannerist architecture in Tuscany characterized by exaggerated proportions, spatial tension, and deliberate distortion of classical forms.

name: Moorish Revival
summary: An architectural style reviving elements of Islamic architecture from North Africa and Spain.

name: Stick Style
summary: A transitional style between Gothic Revival and Queen Anne with exposed structural elements.

name: Nieuwe Bouwen
summary: Dutch modernist architecture emphasizing functionalism, rationalism, and the integration of architecture with social reform.

name: Metabolism
summary: A Japanese architectural movement that envisioned cities as organic, living systems.

name: Critical Regionalism
summary: Architectural approach that seeks to create modern architecture that responds to local context and culture.

name: Vernacular Revival
summary: Architecture that reinterprets traditional local building techniques and forms using contemporary materials and methods.

name: Tulou Hakka Roundhouses
summary: Large, multi-story, communal residences built by Hakka people in mountainous regions of Fujian Province.

name: Kerala architecture
summary: A distinctive architectural style from Kerala featuring sloping roofs, wood carvings, and courtyard layouts.

name: Javanese Joglo
summary: Traditional Javanese vernacular house characterized by its pyramid-shaped roof, central pillar, and hierarchical spatial organization.

name: Scottish baronial
summary: Gothic Revival style incorporating Scottish castle elements.

name: Swahili Coastal Architecture
summary: A distinctive building style along the East African coast blending African, Arab, Persian, and European influences.

name: Ancestral Puebloan Great Houses
summary: Massive stone-walled structures with distinctive D-shaped rooms and planned layouts, representing advanced urban planning in pre-Columbian North America.

name: Fijian Bure
summary: A traditional Fijian dwelling built with natural materials thatched together to form conical roofs.

name: Goan Portuguese Architecture
summary: A unique blend of Portuguese and Indian architectural traditions in former Portuguese Goa.

name: Brezhnevka
summary: A style of mass housing developed during Leonid Brezhnev's rule, featuring larger apartments than Khrushchyovkas but still using prefabricated concrete panels.

name: Gopuram Temple Gate
summary: A monumental towered gateway entrance to Hindu temple complexes, particularly in Dravidian architecture.

name: Shanxi Courtyard Compounds
summary: Large, fortified courtyard residences built by wealthy Shanxi merchants with defensive features.

name: Kalyan Minaret Style
summary: A distinctive tower-like minaret built in 1127 in Bukhara, serving as a prototype for later Central Asian minarets with its massive cylindrical form and decorative brickwork.

name: Kerala timber-roof temples
summary: Distinctive temple architecture from Kerala featuring timber roofs, sloping roofs, and courtyard layouts.

name: Turf-Roofed Farmhouse
summary: A traditional farmhouse construction method using turf or sod as roofing material with stone or timber walls.

name: Lombard Romanesque
summary: Regional variant of Romanesque architecture characterized by decorative brickwork and distinctive bell towers.

name: Byzantine Revival
summary: An architectural style reviving elements of Byzantine architecture from the Eastern Roman Empire.

name: Napier NZ Deco
summary: A distinctive Art Deco style in Napier New Zealand following the 1931 earthquake.
